correctness.rationale: Every nonzero inner-rank-one matrix partitions by common valuation and corresponds bijectively to a primitive rank-one matrix at the residual depth. Primitive outer products have exact unit-scaling stabilizer; finite-character orthogonality yields a closed five-case primitive-layer Fourier transform. Its sum gives every Smith-type adjacency eigenvalue; Smith orbit sizes give all multiplicities and sum to p^(4k). The two explicit negative formulas and positive upper-valutation cases prove the minimum absolute eigenvalue p+1 precisely at invertible frequencies. Independent FFT enumeration through k=4 at p=2 and k=3 at p=3, plus exact formula checks across four primes to k=8, match. This is an all-depth algebraic proof, not inference from finite computation.

value.rationale: A complete closed Fourier spectrum and exact multiplicities for a canonical distance-one rank-metric Cayley graph of size p^(4k) at every depth k>=3 is a natural global invariant, not a routine restatement of orbit counts. The nonzero spectrum and exact smallest absolute eigenvalue p+1 yield a sharp, depth-independent inverse L2 stability theorem, a structural phenomenon of interest to harmonic analysis, spectral graph theory and codes.
